name: Desoto National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all Refuges, be very mindful of impact and footprint. Not many parking lots in this one, and many parking areas are seasonally closed. Visitors center is an option. Entrance fees required.

name: Driftless Area National Wildlife Refuge
notes: Research or call ahead to get info on access to some areas. For example, the Finch Memorial Unit northwest of Decorah is closed to the public to protect wildlife.

name: Iowa Wetland Management District
notes: Several WMAs in Iowa are managed by the Iowa DNR but associated with the federally designated FWS "Iowa Wetland Management District". As such, activations are possible at areas on the US FWS map and several may be two-fers.

name: Neal Smith National Wildlife Refuge
notes: This is a wildlife refuge. Certain areas are restricted or special care is necessary. Additionally during some hunting seasons some areas are heavily used by hunters. Take extreme caution and wear ORANGE

name: Port Louisa National Wildlife Refuge
notes: This is a National Wildlife Refuge, so you are encouraged to check in with Rangers prior, but if not then carefully read the website info, and please observe the "No stakes, no tree/wires, and small footprint" POTA guidance.

name: Union Slough National Wildlife Refuge
notes: Wildlife refuge managed by US FWS. Some nearby land is K-0270, but they do not overlap for a 2-fer.

name: Flint Hills National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all NWRs, practicing a small, non-invasive activating footprint that does not have ANY impact on grounds, trees, wildlife, other visitors, etc., is important to both the NWR and POTA missions. Check-in with NWR Ranger station strongly advised.

notes: As with all NWRs, practicing a small, non-invasive activating footprint that does not have ANY impact on grounds, trees, wildlife, other visitors, etc., is important to both the NWR and POTA missions. Check-in with NWR Ranger station strongly advised.

Big Muddy National Wildlife Refuge
notes: This is a large, multi-tract park. Do your research on Google Earth before attempting...KNOW where you are going! Entire park is a flood plain, and access can be difficult or simple depending on time of year and tract chosen.

name: Clarence Cannon National Wildlife Refuge
notes: This is a refuge, and experience shows that a visit to the ranger station may be the best way to get information about the park. However this ranger station may be far away. Usually no use of trees or stakes.

name: Great River National Wildlife Refuge
notes: This is a refuge and experience shows that a visit to the ranger station may be the best way to get information about the refuge, but regional office is far from park. Usually no use of trees or stakes.

name: Mingo National Wildlife Refuge
notes: Please check the website for most recent closures and restrictions. While not required, activators have benefitted from stopping in a the refuge headquarters or ranger station to discuss local rules.

name: Loess Bluffs National Wildlife Refuge
notes: Nice parking lots, bird-watching lookouts and other facilities. Easy to find. RF quiet, scenic location.

name: Swan Lake National Wildlife Refuge
notes: Large, and typically strictly patrolled by rangers. Activation by mobile preferred, but there are out-of-the-way small open spaces to set up. Park undergoing construction in 2021, but access still OK, last known.

notes: As with all NWRs, practicing a small, non-invasive activating footprint that does not have ANY impact on grounds, trees, wildlife, other visitors, etc., is important to both the NWR and POTA missions. Check-in with NWR Ranger station strongly advised.

notes: Open sunrise to sunset. Office hours Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

name: Missouri National Recreational River National Wild and Scenic River
notes: Part of a river system...more detailed activator research needed for local activation/locations. "From Gavins Point Dam, South Dakota, downstream to Ponca State Park, Nebraska. From Fort Randall Dam to Lewis and Clark Lake."

name: Wilson's Creek National Battlefield
notes: This is generally a busy park. There used to be a fee to enter, but recently the park has become free entry.

name: Gateway Arch National Park
notes: This is a very busy in-town park. Limited parking space and some open areas, but may be difficult to set up without being in the way. Mobile or pedestrian activation suggested at the southern edge of the park across corner of 1st and Poplar Streets.

name: Rocky Creek State Conservation Area
notes: This conservation area has over twenty discontinuous tracts and is intersected by the Ozark State Trail in several locations. Research this park carefully prior to activating.

name: Brown vs. Board of Education National Historic Site
notes: Parking area in front of building.

name: Fort Larned National Historic Site
notes: Available parking.

name: Fort Scott National Historic Site
notes: The best activation spot is the parking lot on the southeast side. Rangers are very protective of the grounds, so virtually no option to activate from the grassy square, buildings, and grounds.

name: Harry S. Truman Family Farm National Historic Site
notes: The park is in a dense commercial area, so QRN has been reported. Large parking lot, as well as a large open grassy field behind the house to set up. The back field is a short (50 yds) walk from the parking lot.

name: Herbert Hoover National Historic Site
notes: Park has a nice green area with a couple shelters across the main street from the main building.

name: Nicodemus National Historic Site
notes: Street parking.

name: Ulysses S. Grant National Historic Site
notes: Tiny parking lot in a dense residential area, under high tension power lines. Not ideal for activation, but can be done with mobile antenna. Can possibly do pedestrian portable in the yard area.

name: Agate Fossil Beds National Monument
notes: Very limited cell coverage.

name: Effigy Mounds National Monument
notes: Park hours are typically sunrise to sunset and closed on holidays. Check the NPS website or call ahead. There are some lookout points along the river bluff that are a higher elevation.

name: George Washington Carver National Monument
notes: There are no fees to access this park, but the parking lot is very large. Visitor center is an interesting tour if you activate during open hours. The gate is generally open round-the-clock, but that may change.

name: Homestead National Historical Park
notes: High noise levels reported recently at this park, especially at the eastern visitor center.

name: Babler Memorial State Park
notes: Full service State Park that can be busy at peak times. Will find yourself driving some time around the roads to find a suitable spot to activate, and settle on an unoccupied campsite or group area.

name: Sam A. Baker State Park
notes: Full service park with many usual facilities, plus equestrian. Picnic, shelters, etc.

name: Bennett Spring State Park
notes: This park is focused on camping and fishing. Generally very busy. Several parking lots, some open spaces, but be aware of foot traffic. Nice restaurant on site, fish hatchery fishing with special permit.

name: Big Lake State Park
notes: Was heavily damaged by flooding but re-opened as a day use only park. Lots of parking lots, open areas, picnic tables, etc. Friendly rangers.

name: Big Oak Tree State Park
notes: Smaller limited services State Park. Noted for hiking trails, shelters, and picnic areas.

name: Big Sugar Creek State Park
notes: Smaller park with hiking trails. This park is remote and the road crosses streams that may be over the bridges and the road can be washed out. Use caution.

name: Castlewood State Park
notes: This park is close to town and can be very busy at peak times. Very busy. Hiking and biking trails, open areas, limited parking.

name: Crowder State Park
notes: Easy to find...primarily a campground park with boating and fishing access. Several parking lots and open areas to activate.

name: Cuivre River State Park
notes: This park gives the impression that it has seen better days, but activation spots are easy to find. Scenic areas are available, as is some fishing.

name: Current River State Park
notes: Smaller historic park with hiking trails and picnic sites.

name: Don Robinson State Park
notes: Primarily a hiking and picnic park. Limited parking areas and limited open areas.

name: Echo Bluff State Park
notes: This is a large full-service State Park that offers year-round activities and accommodation. Offers a lodge.

name: Elephant Rocks State Park
notes: Smaller geologic themed park with hiking trails, picnic areas, and trails designed for people with visual and physical disabilities.

name: Finger Lakes State Park
notes: Full-featured State Park. Several parking lots and various venues for activations. Close to Columbia, so can be busy at peak times.

name: Graham Cave State Park
notes: Nice park, but with widely varying elevations. Parking lot near the ranger station is best, and the rangers are very friendly.

name: Grand Gulf State Park
notes: Primarily a hike and sight-seeing park. Some picnic and open areas, with limited parking.

name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park
notes: Popular day park with many facilities. Several parking lots, open areas, shorelines, shelters, etc. Widely varying elevations around the park.

name: Harry S Truman State Park
notes: Very popular State Park, lots of facilities, but can be very busy at peak times. Also subject to flooding.

name: Hawn State Park
notes: Larger park with very good hiking trails and campground.

name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
notes: Textbook State Park...nice picnic areas, hiking trails, things to see, unusual sights, etc. Hiking trails include the Ozark State Trail that can take you into the ONLY access to Jay Nixon State Park and further east across the State.

name: Jones-Confluence Point State Park
notes: Primarily and hiking and bird-watching park. Limited parking.

name: Katy Trail State Park
notes: This is a "trail park" built on an old railroad bed. There are several "depots" along the trail, so activation is possible from one of the depots or spurs, or from the trail itself, as long as antenna doesn't block trail.

name: Knob Noster State Park
notes: Typical park, parking lots, picnic areas, etc. Some limited shelter space. Terrain elevation varies.

name: Lake of the Ozarks State Park
notes: Large premium State Park. Almost every facility available. The Lee C Fine Airport is in the park (if you step off the apron). Many parking lots, hiking trails, some open spaces, especially along the trails.

name: Lake Wappapello State Park
notes: Larger full-service State Park with all possible activities plus equestrian trails/facilities. Large lake and boating.

name: Lewis and Clark State Park
notes: Small State Park that was devastated during recent floods. Check with the park office for real-time status before before driving out during the spring season. There are several parking lots and a few shelters, park benches.

name: Long Branch State Park
notes: Open areas abound, causeway across the lake. Borders K-5697 (separated by a road) at the north end of the lake.

name: Mark Twain State Park
notes: Typical State with camping, fishing, etc. Several parking lots and open spaces to activate.

name: Meramec State Park
notes: Full service State Park with camping, picnic areas, cabins and a motel.

name: Montauk State Park
notes: Full service park with rooms and cabins with a dining lodge offered for overnight stays.

name: Morris State Park
notes: Primarily a hiking State Park...smaller park with few facilities.

name: Onondaga Cave State Park
notes: Scenic park, picnic areas, parking lots and limited open areas.

name: Pershing State Park
notes: Typical state park...variety of facilities and open spaces or picnic areas. Limited shelters. Easy to find.

name: Pomme de Terre State Park
notes: This is primarily a campground State Park. Oddly very few open areas, parking lots or picnic areas. Several trails around the lake to activate from shorelines or bluffs.

name: Prairie State Park
notes: This is a very open park...and there are roaming bison everywhere. There is a small parking lot on a slight rise on the access road that is the best activating spot, but other spots are available for different setups.

name: Roaring River State Park
notes: This park is in a deep east-west valley between two ridges (open to the east), but activating on both 20 and 40 meters was easy. Several camping, picnic, parking spots available.

name: Robertsville State Park
notes: Campgrounds and picnic areas with some open areas and limited parking at peak times.

name: Rock Bridge Memorial State Park
notes: Typical small State park...several open spaces, picnic areas, limited shelters, walking paths. Popular with dog-walkers so be mindful of walkways.

name: Route 66 State Park
notes: Somewhat of a small park compressed into a highway/commercial area. By far the best activating location is the large, paved boat launch area on the south east end.

name: St. Francois State Park
notes: Larger full service State Park.

name: St. Joe State Park
notes: Many facilities at this park, camping, picnic, equestrian, hiking, fishing, etc. Also an Off-road-Vehicle trail that requires a day permit ranging fro $5 to $10 depending on type of vehicle.

name: Stockton State Park
notes: Nice State Park with many facilities. Note that there are many Corps of Engineers sites around the park/lake that are NOT in K-1786. The islands in the lake are part of the US Islands program.

name: Table Rock State Park
notes: Very scenic park, but be aware that the area has numerous tourist scenic overlooks that are not in the park. Several parking lots, some shelters. Generally a very busy park next door to Branson.

name: Taum Sauk Mountain State Park
notes: The park has a 12-site basic campground, a special-use area for group camping, and a picnic area. This park also includes SOTA sites inside and nearby.

name: Thousand Hills State Park
notes: Full service State Park, but with several parking lots, and picnic areas.

name: Trail of Tears State Park
notes: Nice park, especially nice scenic views of the river from overlooks. Hiking trails, picnic areas, etc.

name: Van Meter State Park
notes: This is primarily a campground park with very large mature trees. Limited parking/picnic areas, almost no open spaces, so antennas will be under trees, although not reportedly been a problem to activate.

name: Wakonda State Park
notes: Full-featured State Park, but not very large. A main parking lot with a few smaller ones and several hiking trails. Fishing is good. Not much day use, so the rangers may be puzzled at just wanting to stay for an hour, but they are friendly.

name: Wallace State Park
notes: Typical park, lots of parking lots, some open spaces. Terrain elevation varies. Campgrounds and limited shelters may be available.

name: Washington State Park
notes: Full-service smaller State Park...no special issues.

name: Watkins Mill State Park
notes: Nice lakeshore park. A walking trail can be activated on foot. Several picnic tables lakeshore, and a larger shelter that isn't usually occupied weekdays.

name: Weston Bend State Park
notes: Popular park for local ham clubs. Several shelters, picnic tables, and hiking trails available. Much of the park is at lower elevation relative to the region.

name: Ambrose A. Call State Park
notes: Camping and picnic areas available for activations in this small state park.

name: Backbone State Park
notes: NOTE: this POTA entity is adjacent to but not within Backbone State Forest (so, not a 2-fer). Nice park & campground.

name: Banner Lakes at Summerset State Park
notes: Several lakes and parking lots. No shelters or convenient picnic tables. Basically, a local fishing hole with some trails.

name: Beed's Lake State Park
notes: Very nice "cozy" State Park...several picnic tables and places to park.

name: Bellevue State Park
notes: Small state park overlooking the Mississippi River. Campground, shelter, and open picnic areas are available for activation possibilities.

name: Big Creek State Park
notes: Nice park with several great activation areas including shelters that may be reserved but are usually available. The largest shelter has power and is located next to the beach.

name: Blackhawk State Park
notes: Campsites, cabins, picnic areas and other possibilities for activations at this small state park.

name: Cedar Rock State Park
notes: Park at a Frank Lloyd Wright home. Open May-Oct. Off-season, contact park mgr (Katie) a few days in advance cedar_rock@dnr.Iowa.gov to use parking lot. If you do, close/latch gate when finished. Don't use stakes. WMA to the NW is also part of the park.

name: Clear Lake State Park
notes: Limited parking, but some nice beachfront picnic areas. A shelter, but research before using it.

name: Elinor Bedell State Park
notes: Located on the east side of East Okoboji Lake, this small park has camping and a shelter. Nice spot to activate.

name: Elk Rock State Park
notes: This is an equestrian park and during camping season is heavily used by horse and rider. No shelter, but activations from campground or boat launch area are feasible.

name: Fort Defiance State Park
notes: Wooded park south of Estherville with shelters, camping and picnic areas for activation opportunities.

name: Geode State Park
notes: Picnic areas, campground and shelters are options for activations at this small park.

name: George Wyth State Park
notes: Park runs along the Cedar River and includes some small lakes. Several parking areas with picnic tables and shelters.

name: Green Valley State Park
notes: State park includes several activation opportunities... camping, shelters, picnic areas.

name: Gull Point State Park
notes: Gull Point State Park is a larger park in the cluster of parks that surround the lakes here. It includes camping, picnic areas and shelters along the lake. https://www.iowadnr.gov/portals/idnr/uploads/parks/parkmaps/gullptmap.pdf

name: Honey Creek State Park
notes: Large lake at this state park with many activation locations including picnic areas, cabins, campgrounds and shelter options. May be busy in summer months.

name: Lacey-Keosauqua State Park
notes: Latitude & Longitude is the coordinates for "Ely Ford crossing" on the bank of the river. This is part of the Mormon Trail US-4573 (2 Fer). A Nice area to spend the day activating The State Park borders with Shimek State Forest on the Eastern Border

name: Lake Ahquabi State Park
notes: Campground and shelters for activation. Reopening in 2023.

name: Lake Anita State Park
notes: Modern state park with camping, shelters, picnic areas and other activation locations available

name: Lake Darling State Park
notes: Nice state park with many locations for activations including shelters, campgrounds, picnic areas and more.

name: Lake Keomah State Park
notes: 2 shelters, campgrounds and several picnic areas provide good activation spots.

name: Lake Macbride State Park
notes: Iowa's largest state park has many places to activate including campgrounds, shelters and picnic areas.

name: Lake Manawa State Park
notes: Large parking lots and open areas on lakeside.

name: Lake of Three Fires State Park
notes: Typical SP with camping, shelters, day use areas.

name: Lake Wapello State Park
notes: State park with several activation options including campground, shelter, cabins, and picnic areas.

name: Lewis and Clark State Park
notes: This park is embedded in a residential area, but park amenities are clearly marked. Easy spots to activate on the lakeshore with picnic tables.

name: Maquoketa Caves State Park
notes: Campground, shelter, and picnic areas for activation options. High bluffs might be considered when activating.

name: McIntosh Woods State Park
notes: Full featured SP across from Clear Lake. Large parking lots, day use areas. Nice lake.

name: Mini-Wakan State Park
notes: One of several tiny State Parks around the lakes. Neat tidy park.

name: Nine Eagles State Park
notes: Nice park with shelters and open spaces. Hiking and fishing also available.

name: Okamanpedan (Tuttle) State Park
notes: The small state park features a shady lakeside picnic area, along with an open shelter available on a first-come, first-served basis.

name: Palisades-Kepler State Park
notes: Nice park along the Cedar River. Shelter, cabin and picnic area activation spots available.

name: Pikes Peak State Park
notes: Very nice park with overlooks of the Mississippi River. Significant closures of the park in 2022 due to renovations. Check the website for details or call ahead.

name: Pikes Point State Park
notes: Picnic tables, a CCC-era stone shelter and a view of West Lake Okoboji make this a nice spot to activate.

name: Pilot Knob State Park
notes: Older SP, but also includes the SOTA Pilot Knob site...easy to access from one of the SP parking lots.

name: Pine Lake State Park
notes: Several shelters are available (may be reserved). Easy to access this state park from the town of Eldora, just off the highway.

name: Prairie Rose State Park
notes: Campgrounds, cabins, and shelters are available for activations at this typical, quiet State Park.

name: Preparation Canyon State Park
notes: Quiet, a bit overgrown, but well-maintained park...narrow paved roads. Several potential activating spots.

name: Red Haw State Park
notes: Very nice park with several open areas, picnic and camping areas around a lake. Shelter is a great spot to activate at this park.

name: Rice Lake State Park
notes: Nice park, well-maintained. Several activation options.

name: Rock Creek State Park
notes: A bathroom facility is located next to the East shelter house. West shelter is on a hill overlooking the lake Bike Access: 5.7 mile asphalt bike trail from Grinnell Iowa to the park entrance.

name: Springbrook State Park
notes: Outstanding park with a picnic area up on higher, level ground with decent cell service. Very well maintained full service state park.

name: Stone State Park
notes: Several activating spots, with elevated scenic outlooks...this is an edge-of-town park.

name: Trappers Bay State Park
notes: Rough around the edges, but lots of primitive parking, dirt roads, etc. Good place to fish, otherwise not a "destination" park.

name: Twin Lakes State Park
notes: Shelters and picnic areas provide opportunities for activations at this small state park.

name: Union Grove State Park
notes: Shelter on west side of lake is reservable. Picnic tables and parking in several spots around park. Campground on south side is within the park. Typically, this is a quiet park.

name: Viking Lake State Park
notes: Nice State Park...lots of activating spots.

name: Walnut Woods State Park
notes: Smaller but nice park close to town with several open areas, parking lots, and a variety of other activities available. The only shelter is a lodge that must be reserved for access, but there are plenty of picnic tables available.

name: Wapsipinicon State Park
notes: State park with campground, shelter and picnic areas for activations.

name: Waubonsie State Park
notes: A vehicle pass may be required for non-residents. Smaller parking lots and hilly terrain. Can be busy at peak times.

name: Wild Cat Den State Park
notes: Beautiful state park with several activation options including campground, open shelters and picnic areas.

name: Cedar Bluff State Park
notes: Park office is open Mon. - Fri. 8AM - 4PM year round.

name: Cheney State Park
notes: Park office hours: 8:00-4:30, Mon. through Fri.

name: Clinton State Park
notes: Larger State Park with several parking lots and open areas. Can be activated several times and not use the same location twice. Park rangers are friendly. Note that Kansas State Parks have a $5 car day pass fee.

name: Crawford State Park
notes: Park office: 8:00-4:30 Mon.-Sat. - $5 auto day pass fee

name: Cross Timbers State Park
notes: Park office: 8:00-4:30 Mon. through Fri. - $5 auto day pass

name: Eisenhower State Park
notes: Park office: 8:00-4:00 Mon.-Fri. - $5 auto day pass

name: El Dorado State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:30 - $5 auto day pass

name: Elk City State Park
notes: A uniquely scenic and nice park. Unique rotating sheltered picnic tables offer wind and sun shelter. Recommend this park for first activations. Friendly rangers. Note that Kansas State Parks require a $5 day pass for vehicles.

name: Fall River State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:30 - $5 auto day pass

name: Glen Elder State Park
notes: Nice full service state park next door to the GE Wildlife Area, but not a 2-fer.

name: Hillsdale State Park
notes: Smaller park, but several parking areas and some shelters. The shelter that is east of the archery range is a good activating location. Note that Kansas State Parks have a $5 day car pass fee.

name: Kaw River State Park
notes: No access fee

name: Kanopolis Lake State Park
notes: Park office : M-F 8:00 am - 4:00 pm - $5 auto day pass

name: Lovewell State Park
notes: Full service State Park...many activation spots.

name: Meade State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:00 - $5 auto day pass

name: Milford State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:00 - $5 auto day pass

name: Mushroom Rock State Park
notes: No fee

name: Perry State Park
notes: Several parking areas, camping areas, and open spaces.

name: Pomona State Park
notes: Park office Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:00 - $5 auto day pass

name: Prairie Dog State Park
notes: Park office:Mon. Sat. 8:00-4:30 - $5 auto day pass

name: Prairie Spirit Trail State Trail
notes: Garnett Trailhead (across from the Santa Fe Railroad Depot).

name: Sandhills State Park
notes: $5 auto day pass

name: Tuttle Creek State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:30 - $5 auto day pass

name: Webster State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:00 - $5 auto day pass

name: Wilson State Park
notes: Park office: Mon.-Fri. 8:00-4:00 - $5 auto day pass

name: Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park
notes: Park open May to mid-October, see schedule on the website. Admission fee is charged in addition to a valid NE parks permit.

name: Ash Hollow State Park
notes: Park has two units. K-4566 and K-4576 traverse the park - see official maps for possible multi-entity activation.

name: Arbor Lodge State Historical Park
notes: Managed and operated by the Arbor Day Foundation. The park grounds are open year-round and a park permit is not required to enter. Can be busy and crowded at peak times.

name: Bowring Ranch State Historical Park
notes: Park grounds open 9 AM to 5 PM year round.

name: Buffalo Bill Ranch State Historical Park
notes: Open 8 AM - sunset year round.

name: Chadron State Park
notes: Some trails extend outside of park boundaries - see official maps. Park located inside K-3371.

name: Eugene T. Mahoney State Park
notes: Full-featured State Park with all amenities. Vehicle pass/fee required and can be purchased on site.

name: Fort Hartsuff State Historical Park
notes: Park grounds open 8 AM to sunset year round.

name: Fort Kearny State Historical Park
notes: Park grounds open 8 AM to sunset year round.

name: Niobrara State Park
notes: K-0675 and K-4572 go along part of the park border - triple activation possible with proper station placement.

name: Ponca State Park
notes: K-0675 and K-4572 go along part of the park border - triple activation possible with proper station placement.

name: Rock Creek Station State Historical Park
notes: K-4578 goes through the park - dual activation possible with proper station placement. Park does NOT share land with the adjoining K-9366.

name: Smith Falls State Park
notes: Camping season is May 1 to Sept 30. The park remains open for day use year round. K-5622 goes through the park - dual activation possible with proper station placement.

name: Union Grove State Park
notes: Year-round. Between Oct. 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets and other water systems may be closed

name: Arrow Rock State Historic Site
notes: Lots of open spaces, several parking lots, and several other facilities available.

name: Battle of Athens State Historic Site
notes: This is a historic site with buildings. Open areas and building areas may be limited and busy at peak times.

name: Battle of Carthage State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park with some parking areas, very limited shelters, some open spaces. Busy on week-ends, not busy weekdays.

name: Battle of Island Mound State Historic Site
notes: A park out in the middle of open farmland. Very well cared for and clean. Typically activated from the parking lot, but can be activated on foot. Not usually busy. Mostly low QRN, but some cattle fences in the county have been heard.

name: Battle of Lexington State Historic Site
notes: Activation is possible from the tiny parking pull-off. The battlefield can be the best place to activate if you have portable equipment. Some limited park benches, but best to be self-sufficient.

name: Battle of Pilot Knob State Historic Site
notes: This is a historic site. Picnic and hiking trails.

name: Bollinger Mill State Historic Site
notes: Check website for recent status and temporary closures for construction/improvements. Historic site, few services.

name: Boone's Lick State Historic Site
notes: Very remote location. Far from nearest stop sign and no cell service. Otherwise, parking lot is gravel and large. Site is maintained.

name: Bothwell Lodge State Historic Site
notes: Nice parking lots, lots of open spaces, picnic tables.

name: Clark's Hill/Norton State Historic Site
notes: Remote location, but fair-sized parking lot at a trail head. Several private drives in vicinity, so minding private land is important.

name: Confederate Memorial State Historic Site
notes: Textbook park...small parking lots, picnic areas, tall trees, open spaces, etc.

name: Deutschheim State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park. You must park on the street and carry equipment to a park bench to activate.

name: Dillard Mill State Historic Site
notes: Several parking lots and nice picnic shelters, as well as open spaces.

name: Felix Vallé House State Historic Site
notes: Limited parking and open areas. Can be busy at peak times.

name: First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park with limited parking or access. Need to ask rangers for access to back yard for activation.

name: Gen. John J. Pershing Boyhood Home State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park. There is a parking lot, and a large open space north-west of the home buildings. Rangers are friendly and will allow you to set up on the open space grass.

name: Gov. Daniel Dunklin's Grave State Historic Site
notes: Very limited parking. Do not activate within the gates.

name: Hunter-Dawson State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town site. Limited grounds available. Research the website and Google Earth before activating. Have a plan before you leave.

name: Iliniwek Village State Historic Site
notes: Small park with large circle parking lot, hiking trail, something looking like a shelter. Power lines nearby, but noise is not too bad.

name: Jewell Cemetery State Historic Site
notes: This is a small site on a very busy main trafficway and commercial/apartment area. Small parking lot. Please do NOT activate from inside the cemetery.

name: Locust Creek Covered Bridge State Historic Site
notes: The park must be accessed on foot by crossing the footbridge. The area around the historic covered bridge is about 1/4 mile hike, and has benches and an open area.

name: Mark Twain Birthplace State Historic Site
notes: Scenic and well-maintained site. It is listed on the State website separately from K-1772 so should be activated separately.

name: Mastodon State Historic Site
notes: Parking, picnic and hiking available, but can be very busy at peak times.

name: Missouri Mines State Historic Site
notes: Limited parking or open areas, may be very busy at peak times.

name: Missouri State Museum/Jefferson Landing State Historic Site
notes: This is a tight spot in-town site. Mobile activation or pedestrian activations are best. Very few open areas.

name: Nathan Boone Homestead State Historic Site
notes: This is a smaller out-of-the-way park with limited hours. Plan your activation accordingly. Technically, the entrance gate is set back on the park land and is "in" the park, but you may be blocking the entrance.

name: Osage Village State Historic Site
notes: Quiet, out-of-the-way park. Nice parking lot to activate from, at least one picnic table next to the parking lot, and a hiking trail for pedestrian activations.

name: Sandy Creek Covered Bridge State Historic Site
notes: Very limited parking or open areas, and can be busy at peak times.

name: Sappington Cemetery State Historic Site
notes: This site is in the middle of open farmlands and at the end of a gravel road. The parking lot is part of the park, so that is the only spot to activate from. Please do NOT activate from inside the cemetery perimeter.

name: Scott Joplin House State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park. No on-site parking. May be allowed to set up in back yard access from the laneway, but need to inquire prior.

name: Thomas Hart Benton Home and Studio State Historic Site
notes: This is a city-center residential area museum with very small acreage. The park rangers are very friendly and may let you come in the driveway to operate mobile. You can also set up in the garden areas. The front street/curb is not within the park.

name: Towosahgy State Historic Site
notes: This is primarily an archeological site. Parking lot activating.

name: Union Covered Bridge State Historic Site
notes: At the end of the county road, somewhat remote. A small grassy area to park.

name: Watkins Woolen Mill State Historic Site
notes: Technically, K-1795 and K-3368 are the same park...with K-3368 being "surrounded" by K-1795. They appear separately in the State Park website listing, so they should be activated as separate parks. The Woollen mill parking lot is small.

name: Bryant Creek State Park
notes: This park has recently been developed and opened to public access. It has very nice activating spots, ample parking, well-developed trails, and outhouse...well marked.

name: Eleven Point State Park
notes: This park is indicated as being closed, but experiences with other Missouri parks (three others) of this status indicate ranger willingness to allow gate activation or hike-in day use.

name: Nebraska National Forest
notes: Entity has two sections: Sandhills (near Chadron) and Halsey (near Halsey).

name: Samuel R McKelvie National Forest
notes: Beware of flooded roads - check website for latest information. Does not share land with K-5631.

name: Chimney Rock National Historic Site
notes: No trails are traversing the entity - no multi-entity activation possible.

name: Schilling Wildlife Management Area
notes: Open to public from April 1 through October 14 from 7 AM to 9 PM. Access may be challenging due to recent flooding damage.

name: Jensen Lagoon National Waterfowl Production Area
Moger National Waterfowl Production Area
notes: This park includes both Moger and Alberding which is less than a mile north. These were combined but POTA has left them separate.

name: DeSoto (NE) National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all NWRs, practicing a small, non-invasive activating footprint that does not have ANY impact on grounds, trees, wildlife, other visitors, etc., is important to both the NWR and POTA missions. Check-in with NWR Ranger station strongly advised.

name: Alberding Lagoon National Wildlife Management Area
notes: Combined with Moger less than a mile south, but POTA has left them separate.

name: Smith Lagoon National Waterfowl Production Area
Lake Wanahoo State Recreation Area
notes: NE Park Permits not valid. Daily entry permit $5.

name: Willa Cather Memorial Prairie State Historic Site
notes: Circle parking lot with wider spots to activate. Relatively higher elevation.

name: Nine Mile Prairie National Historical Park
Chapel View Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Nice prairie park setting with two parking lots, but with one caution and one advisory. Caution that on the county road about 1 mile from the park, there are two or three very large dogs that chase cars. The park has reports of heavy RF noise.

name: Tallgrass Prairie Preserve National Conservation Area
notes: Visitor Center closed. Park rangers stationed in the Historic House

name: Paris Springs State Conservation Area
notes: There is only one parking lot and no other activation spots other than if you hike in and set up in a forest clearing. The driveway to the parking lot fords a stream that may be higher water than the bridge. Caution. No park signage...use the map.

name: Trail of Tears National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Ozark National Wild and Scenic River
notes: A scenic river primarily for float trips, but several launches and take-outs along the river. Research the site and Google Earth for an activating spot before you go. Check website for seasonal water conditions or flooding.

name: Heron Haven State Park
notes: Small gravel parking lot next to a busy mini-mall/office complex. Under power lines. The gate to the parking lot closes at dusk.

name: Chalco Hills State Recreation Area
notes: Park trails are connected to the Omaha area hike/bike trail system.

name: Elkhorn Crossing State Park
notes: The park is open April 1 through November 1. Check https://www.papionrd.org/river-access-sites-open-or-closed-check-here/ for current status.

name: Platte River Landing State Park
notes: Day-use only. Open from April 1 through November 1. Check https://www.papionrd.org/recreation/river-access/ for current status.

name: Lincoln Saline Wetland State Park
notes: This is on the edge of town, but quiet spot. The circle parking lot is inside the park so OK to activate. If you hike into the park past the fence, be prepared/protected for ticks, during warmer weather seasons.

name: Buckley Creek State Recreation Area
notes: Quiet smaller park, somewhat remote with camping and a lake. Outside of peak times, has ample parking and open areas around the south and east shores of the lake. Well-maintained.

name: Liberty Cove State Recreation Area
notes: Quiet smaller lake park with camping facilities. Suggest that the road from the east be used to get to the park. The road west of the park can be in rough shape.

name: Prairie Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Larger park with good activation spots. Can be busy at times.

name: Roseland Lake State Recreation Area
notes: This park looks like it has seen better days. Gives the impression of having been abandoned. Evidence of dumping and other non-park activities. Easy enough to activate, the entrance is easy to miss...a choice between a dirt road and another dirt road.

name: Bear Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Open, flat, good parking lots.

name: Big Indian State Recreation Area
notes: Nice open area park, good parking lots and lakeside activating spots.

name: Clatonia State Recreation Area
notes: Can have very high noise levels due to local industries/shops.

name: Cub Creek (southern) State Recreation Area
notes: Another entity with a similar name exists at a different location (US-12337).

name: Willard L. Meyer State Recreation Area
Wolf-Wildcat Wildlife Management Area
notes: Good roads, good parking lots, out of the way.

name: Upper Mississippi River National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all NWR's always a good idea to check with the ranger's office before activating to get the most recent info and suggestions for easiest access. POTA park pin is at the Winona Ranger Office but park is 260+ miles long.

name: Pleasant Creek State Recreation Area
notes: Lake with campground. Activation areas include parking areas with boat ramps, shelter, picnic areas, and campground.

name: Mines of Spain State Recreation Area
notes: Parking, picnic, and shelter areas for activation - scenic area of Dubuque along the Mississippi River.

name: Mark Twain National Forest
notes: This forest is very large and has several discontinuous tracts spanning almost the entire state. Research before activating. Large variety of accesses, lots, waterways, etc.

name: Custer Gallatin National Forest
notes: This listing reflects the combining of Custer and Gallatin National Forests. K-4503, the old Gallatin NF listing, has been archived and can no longer be activated. Activations and contacts from old listing remain in your account. K0HAA

name: California National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Mormon Pioneer National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Oregon National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Pony Express National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Santa Fe National Historic Trail
notes: This is a Trail park, and may intersect other Trails, and/or pass through public, State and/or National parks. Research the park Trail map as well as Google Earth to locate an activating area that is within 100 feet of the trail AND on public lands.

name: Harry S. Truman Birthplace State Historic Site
notes: An in-town park with very little open area. Best to activate from mobile. Not many options.

name: World War I Museum National Memorial
notes: The front lawn area has many picnic tables and trees. Weekends often have special events that occupy the entire lawn. Otherwise, this park has been activated numerous times. Some rangers/docents are hams/friendly.

name: Barkley Memorial State Forest
notes: Many 3rd party websites list this as a "state park". At best it is an abandoned public property that has received a "Barkley State Forest Parking Lot" sign. At dead end of a road, with some private property in vicinity.

name: Gifford State Forest
notes: DNR forester confirms Gifford is OPEN. Some tourist websites incorrectly report that it is closed. No in boundary parking, hike-in park activation only. No trails or clearings available - so be prepared.

name: Holst State Forest
notes: The forest begins at the end of a muddy 1/2 mile dirt road. Parking for maybe two vehicles at a trail head into the forest.

name: Loess Hills State Forest
notes: This forest has several tracts separated by several miles. Conveniently, the access to both the Preparation Canyon State Park and this forest is at a fork in the road.

name: Pilot Mound State Forest
notes: Small SF within Boone and Yellow forests. Must do homework before finding this one.

name: Shimek State Forest
notes: State forest is divided into 5 units. Camping is available. Several areas to activate in each unit.

name: Stephens State Forest
notes: Easy enough to find the official sign, but roads into the forest are narrow and unimproved, so best wait for dry weather. Some lumber cutting activity in certain areas of the park. Primitive campground has picnic tables.

name: White Pine Hollow State Forest
notes: Note this entity is White Pine Hollow State Forest which borders White Pine Hollow State Preserve. Access road (White Pine Lane) from the south.

name: Yellow River State Forest
notes: Yellow River State Forest is comprised of several distributed "units". Nice park with a variety of places to activate. It is adjacent to Effigy Mounds National Monument K-0922 to the south.

name: Busiek State Forest
notes: Much of this park is at lower elevations and the main parking lot is under the highway overpass. Some hiking trails to higher elevations on the western side. Large shooting range and equestrian activity.

name: Lester R. Davis Memorial State Forest
notes: Literally across the road from Prairie State Park, this is a small parking lot, a sign, and a big rock. Easy and obvious to find.

name: Reifsnider State Forest
notes: Dense forest and a large shooting range. Generally busy park, especially at peak times. Elevations vary widely, but tend to get lower as you go further into the park. Enough room near the entrance to activate/park.

name: Vanderhoef (Archie and Gracie) Memorial State Forest
notes: Small park with one parking lot and circle turnaround, and a few hiking trails. Easy to find, good signage.

name: Murphy (John F.) Memorial State Forest
notes: Primarily a wildlife area. Small parking lot on a county road, easy to spot. Can also hike inland to activate. don't be frightened...this park is on a regular low-altitude training route for A-10's from the nearby AF base.

name: Rand Bar Wildlife Management Area
notes: Bordered by private lands, the Missouri River, and the Desoto NWR, the only "normal access" would be to hike 0.75 mile from Desoto NWR. Note that off-road areas of Desoto NWR are seasonally closed, so check Desoto website for access dates. See DNR map.

name: Niobrara National Wild and Scenic River
Sherman Reservoir State Recreation Area
notes: Park has several spacious parking lots on the south side at good elevation overlooking the lake.

name: White Nursery State Forest
notes: Developed, operating state tree nursery. A few parking lots along main road through the park.

name: Holland State Forest
notes: This park has only one parking spot, and it is at the bottom of a valley with over 100ft walls. Feels dark on a sunny day. You can also hike to the top of the hill to activate at higher elevation.

name: Funk Memorial State Forest
notes: This park has three separate tracts. Research carefully on Google Earth before activating to know where you will go.

name: Fisher Grove State Park
notes: Year-round. Between Oct. 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets and other water systems may be closed

name: Spirit Mound Historic Prairie State Park
notes: No entrance fee required.

name: Olive Creek Lake State Recreation Area
Wagon Train Lake State Recreation Area
Lake Minatare State Recreation Area
notes: Closed to public access from October 15 to January 15. Does not share land with K-0445.

name: Standing Bear Lake State Recreation Area
Lake Zorinsky State Park
notes: Connected to Omaha walk/bike trail system. Day use only.

name: Alexandria Lakes State Recreation Area
notes: Nice park. Vehicle entry fee required.

name: Box Butte Reservoir State Recreation Area
Red Willow Reservoir State Recreation Area
Verdon Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Side road-side lake park with several good activating spots.

name: Angeline State Conservation Area
notes: This is a smaller park with scenic lookouts, trails, and equestrian.

name: Atlanta Wildlife Area
notes: Numerous parking lots and roads around the lake.

name: Blind Pony State Conservation Area
notes: Scenic lake, easy to find...two main parking areas, with some shoreline open areas and picnic tables.

name: August A. Busch Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: No lack of activating spots. Numerous small lakes with parking lots. Hiking trails and archery range.

name: Grand Pass State Conservation Area
notes: Large wetlands park with numerous parking lots, BUT the levees and wetlands are constantly changing so only the eastern parking lots are stable from season to season.

name: Fountain Grove State Conservation Area
notes: Expansive area of lakes and wetlands. Several causeways across the park. Several parking lots.

name: Hartell (Ronald and Maude) State Conservation Area
notes: Depending on time of year or week, this is a quaint, smaller park with smaller lakes and several parking lots. Some picnic areas. Campground. Fishing is pretty good as well.

name: Hunnewell Lake State Conservation Area
notes: A very scenic, peaceful lake park with very nice shorelines and several parking lots around the perimeter of the park. A few grassy fishing jetties that can be activated.

name: Indian Trail State Conservation Area
notes: Forested, roads, occasional parking lots. Research on Google Earth before activating.

name: Lake Paho State Conservation Area
notes: A short and a long road on east and west shores respectively. The long road has the higher elevations and better parking lots. Good shoreline areas for activating and fishing.

name: Little Dixie Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Very nice lake park with two large parking areas. Nice open shoreline areas.

name: Lost Valley State Fish and Wildlife Area
notes: This area has been subject to changes as to its status. The State website doesn't say anything, but tourist sites say it is closed. There are parking lots on the bluff and outside the main gate that are inside the park. Research the park.

name: Montrose State Conservation Area
notes: Modest park, with several parking lots and some primitive camping. Good activating site on the southern shoreline boat launch area.

name: Nodaway State Conservation Area
notes: Many perimeter parking lots and boat launches. There is a parking lot on the west border road that is an elevated overlook of the entire park. Good activating spot.

name: Platte Falls State Conservation Area
notes: Research and KNOW where you are going before activating. Many access points and parking lots around the large perimeter. Some may be very isolated. Also has archery and shotgun ranges, and the river is floatable.

name: Pony Express Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Nice smaller lake park. Easy access. Lots of maintained lakeshore to set up. A few parking lots. Fishing is easy access.

name: James A. Reed Memorial Wildlife Area
notes: Tends to be a training park for the state, so new agents may question occasionally. The key is having a small footprint! Lots of parking lots overlooking lakes!

name: Jay Nixon State Park
notes: This is one of four Missouri parks that have not been developed. Experience shows that rangers allow hiking in and out for day use. Currently, Jay Nixon can ONLY be reached via the Ozark Trail...approx 11 mile challenging roundtrip hike from Shut-Ins SP.

name: Shepherd of the Hills State Park
notes: This is one of four Missouri parks that have not been developed. Experience shows that rangers allow hiking in and out for day use or gate activations. Name changed May 2022 from Ozark Mountain.

name: Roger Pryor Pioneer Backcountry State Park
notes: This is primarily a backcountry hiking park.

name: Bruce R. Watkins Cultural Heritage Center State Park
notes: This is a city-center site and is essentially a concrete parking lot for the museum. Automobile activation or very limited footprint...no choice. Busy, high-visibility spot.

name: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park
notes: Good sized parking lot for activation. May be activated on foot via marked trails only.

name: Flint Hills Trail State Park
notes: Research the park to find the best location for your activation before leaving. The Osawatomie trail head has limited parking, but can be acceptable during low activity times.

name: Badger Creek State Recreation Area
notes: Open park with several parking lots, fields, nice lake. Not much development.

name: Blood Run State Historic Site
notes: Historic site with no amenities along the Big Sioux River. Small gravel parking area maybe best. Take care if activating elsewhere.

name: Brushy Creek State Recreation Area
notes: Nice park, feels more like a State Park...lots of good activating options.

name: Emerson Bay State Recreation Area
notes: Small park with neat picnic areas and parking lots.

name: Fairport State Recreation Area
notes: Very small park with campground and boat launch along Mississippi.

name: Fort Atkinson State Preserve
notes: Small, historic abandon military fort with limited activation locations.

name: Lower Gar State Recreation Area
notes: Small drive-through park. Several parking lots and picnic areas.

name: Templar State Recreation Area
notes: Small State Rec Area. Lots of parking and nice grounds for activating options.

name: Volga River State Recreation Area
notes: Park has two campgrounds. Several trails meander through the park and parking scattered throughout park. There is a shelter near the boat ramp by Volga Lake.

name: Wilson Island State Recreation Area
notes: This park's access is at the intersection of the Southern entrance to the Desoto NWR. Basic park with usual amenities.

name: Bixby State Preserve
notes: Single parking lot, with an old shelter next to a stream.

name: Little River Wildlife Management Area
notes: Research carefully before activating. Lots of private land in between public accesses.

name: Ferguson Herold State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller park with only one small gravel parking lot. Popular with deer hunters. Nothing unique, but can be dusty with an east wind.

name: Burr Oak Woods State Conservation Area
notes: An in-town park...large and well-maintained...lots of parking lots, trails. Can be busy at peak hours.

name: Lone Jack Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Primarily a fishing park, large paved parking lot on lakeshore. Possible to set up on a lake jetty. https://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/places/lone-jack-lake-conservation-area

name: Anita B Gorman Discovery Center State Conservation Area
notes: Not to be confused with the nearby city park bearing the same name. This is very downtown Kansas City, not far from the Plaza. Parking lot and a walking path with park benches. Surprisingly low RF noise.

name: Guy B Park State Conservation Area
notes: Essentially one parking lot on one small lake. There are two other small perimeter parking lots. Popular fishing spot.

name: Kendzora State Conservation Area
notes: Only two small parking lots on the county road. Generally quiet, open, low local traffic. Marshland and wildlife.

name: Cooley Lake State Conservation Area
notes: At least four possible activating spots, perhaps more. The easiest is next to the "red barn" if you follow the signs. There is a good elevated spot on the northern bluff, as well. Easy to hike onto the lake jetties also.

name: Amarugia Highlands State Conservation Area
notes: The county roads to and from can be challenging by season, but the park is well-maintained. Several very open parking lots with boat ramps and fishing access.

name: Maple Leaf Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Close to town/highway, primarily a fishing park...large parking lot and boat launching area. Easy to activate.

name: Crooked River State Conservation Area
notes: Somewhat sketchy roads, and basic rolling woodland/field setting. Out-of-the-way, with not much cell service.

name: Poague Haysler State Conservation Area
notes: Several lake causeways and several primitive parking areas. Need to pick your activating sots. Good fishing.

name: Harmony Mission Lake State Conservation Area
notes: The county roads get worse and worse, until you break out to a beautiful park, lake and large paved parking lot with fishing and boat access.

name: Schell-Osage State Conservation Area
notes: Two lakes, but the northern lake has most of the parking areas. Be aware that seasonal flooding can bury the northern-most parking lots and roads. Good camping and fishing.

name: King Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Quiet lake park with a few perimeter parking lots and one boat launch lot. Nice place.

name: Lamine River State Conservation Area
notes: Has a "work-in-progress" feel to it. some good open areas and parking lots off new and old Hwy 50. Primitive area with turkey buzzards circling overhead as you activate...

name: Happy Holler Lake State Conservation Area
notes: this park has two tracts...one that is very primitive and roads will quickly exceed ability of most vehicles. The other contains Happy Holler lake...well-developed and large paved parking area and boat launch. Google Maps may take you the other tract.

name: Ben Branch Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Two parking lots to activate from...one on the west bluff and another near the boat ramp. Very scenic lake.

name: Apple Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Larger conservation area with several parking lots, and a DIY shooting range.

name: Duck Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Adjacent to K-0377 Mingo Refuge. Check website for periodic closures for feral hog eradication activity.

name: Howell Island State Conservation Area
notes: This park only has one parking lot at the trail head that leads to the bridge to the island. Check flooding reports to see if the island is accessible, or just activate at the parking lot.

name: Daniel Boone State Conservation Area
notes: Basic park with gravel roads and parking areas.

name: Peck Ranch State Conservation Area
notes: Very large area with access by both trail and roads...variety of land features, fence lines and other barriers. Research carefully before activating.

name: Weldon Spring State Conservation Area
notes: Primarily a hiking/biking trail park, limited parking areas or open areas. Next to K-5699 a mile or two down the road.

name: General Watkins State Conservation Area
notes: Several parking areas, but check map for closest to highway.

name: Columbia Bottom State Conservation Area
notes: Extensively damaged by flooding. Check website for specific closures and road surface cautions. Research and/or call ahead...not a straightforward park activation.

name: Little Black State Conservation Area
notes: This area has three separate tracts with only one main parking area in the western tract. Also has an archery range.

name: Otter Slough State Conservation Area
notes: This is primarily a wetland area. Check website for updates. Parking lots are roadside to the main north-south road. Several private tracts on the west side of the main road.

name: Coon Island State Conservation Area
notes: Many wetlands, ditches, and a river with primitive camping.

name: Current River State Conservation Area
notes: Very large conservation area with a shooting range. Several parking lots. Also some private lots in the area.

name: Huzzah State Conservation Area
notes: Several access roads and parking lots. Also a DIY shooting range.

name: Meramec State Conservation Area
notes: Primarily a hiking and equestrian trails park. Several parking lots.

name: Lake Girardeau State Conservation Area
notes: Nice lake park with two parking lots and access points. Clean, accessible, well-developed.

name: Castor River State Conservation Area
notes: This area has six separate tracts, some that are walk-in only. The southern tract has the most parking lots and DIY shooting range.

name: Magnolia Hollow State Conservation Area
notes: Only one access road and several parking and picnic areas.

name: Millstream Gardens State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller park with a few central parking lots and an archery range. There is a private tract in the middle of the park, so caution on trespassing if you wander off the beaten path.

name: Diggs-Marshall State Conservation Area
notes: Park with two lakes, nice parking areas and open areas. Good fishing and shorelines.

name: Whetstone Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Very nice multiple lake park with expansive parking areas, DIY shooting range, and good fishing.

name: Rebel's Cove State Conservation Area
notes: Several access points and parking lots around several small lakes/pools. Somewhat lower elevation that surrounding region.

name: Rinquelin Trail Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Very scenic lake, nice parking lot and camping area just north of the lake for activation.

name: Painted Rock State Conservation Area
notes: A few roads and parking lots. Main parking next to small lake next to clubhouse. Can be busy/crowed at peak times.

name: Bois D'Arc State Conservation Area
notes: Larger park with several parking lots around a very irregular perimeter. Look out for private land.

name: Rocky Fork Lakes State Conservation Area
notes: Nice lake park with good parking lots and open areas. Easy to find. Can be busy at peak times.

name: Locust Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Lots of wetlands, and sometimes busy with logging or geophysical work...roads come and go as far as condition. Parking lots on the west and south borders typically reliable.

name: Poosey State Conservation Area
notes: A mosaic of roads, lakes, private tracts, many parking lots, woodland, prairie, etc. Plan your route on Google Earth or you can go in circles. Fishing, and a very nice DIY shooting range on site.

name: Big Buffalo Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Somewhat wild and unimproved. There are two separate tracts of land in this park. Most of the park is at lower elevation. Best parking lot is on the north-western tip of the eastern tract.

name: Bob Brown State Conservation Area
notes: Featureless park...straightforward parking lots, some unimproved open spaces. Know to flood during some years. Check website.

name: Manito Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Huge gravel parking lot next to fishing lake. Nice shelter, but can be busy at peak times.

name: Diana Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Expansive flood plain park. Good levee activation location overlooking the plain.

name: Fiery Fork State Conservation Area
notes: Not many features. three or four parking lots along the main access road.

name: Prairie Home State Conservation Area
notes: Large park, but really only the area around the north-western Johnson Lake is developed. Large parking lot and some open areas. Good fishing.

name: Grand Trace State Conservation Area
notes: Large prairie area with two nice parking lots. park roads get sketchy if you wander any further.

name: Shawnee Trail State Conservation Area
notes: Somewhat primitive area, with primitive camping and fishing. Pine Oak Lake off 50th RD is the best developed area. Huge open areas.

name: Emmett and Leah Seat Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: Large prairie park with several roads and parking lots.

name: Thurnau State Conservation Area
notes: This area was severely devastated by the floods in recent years, but reportedly repaired. Best to research the park before activating.

name: Eagle Bluffs State Conservation Area
notes: The website map is more complex than reality...some parking lots may not be accessible and bird areas may be closed. Parking lots available on the county roads.

name: Bilby Ranch Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Expansive open prairie rolling hills park. Several parking lots at hill crests. Fishing lake. Not usually very busy.

name: Rudolf Bennitt State Conservation Area
notes: As scenic a lake in Missouri as you can find. Very large paved parking lot and boat ramp. Shoreline open areas, good fishing, and a DIY shooting range.

name: Thomas Hill Reservoir State Conservation Area

notes: Parking, boat ramp.

name: Cimarron National Grassland
notes: Vast area of Southwest Kansas bordering Colorado. Various outdoor activities. Auto tour provides access to interpretive sites, picnic areas, toilets, etc. See website.

name: Fox Valley State Conservation Area
notes: Three separate tracts with a lake and a shooting range. Several parking lots.

name: Frost Island State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller area with a few parking lots. Check website for status in case of flooding.

name: Danville State Conservation Area
notes: Irregularly shaped park with roads and some parking lots.

name: Saeger Woods State Conservation Area
notes: Note that this park CANNOT be activated from the Jerry Smith Park parking lot. Approx 1/4 mile hike on the path to K-7500, and then need to step off the path to the west into the woods to be in the park.

name: Belcher Branch Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Quiet lake with very large paved parking lot, boat launch, fishing shoreline open areas.

name: A. Busch Jr at Four Rivers Wetland Reserve
notes: This place is large and easy to get lost. Google Maps is useless here. Plan your route on Google Earth, and KNOW where you want to go. Several interlaced private lands, so be careful not to trespass.

name: Bushwacker Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Scenic prairie lake with several good parking areas and open areas on the west shore of the lake.

name: Baltimore Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Quiet, out-of-the-way park. At least three roads to three parking lots.

name: Bismarck State Conservation Area
notes: Nice lake with three parking lots. There is a campground but check closures on the website. Campsite has been closed due to public abuse.

name: Marshall Junction State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller park with a fe parking lots and a DIY shooting range.

name: Schifferdecker Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: Simple parking lot available at the entrance next to the sign. Easy to find. Some other open spaces and small parking lots further into the park, but lower elevations.

name: White Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller area with a lake and main parking area and boat ramp. Additional parking lots on the southern border road.

name: Settle's Ford State Conservation Area
notes: Large extensive collection of prairie, wetlands, former farms, and other tracts. Several access points and parking lots.

name: Bridger State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller urban park with two parking lots. Close to town and good spot for a first activation attempt.

name: Bluffwoods State Conservation Area
notes: Dense woods op on the bluff. Limited number of parking spots. Somewhat remote, but the parking lots are decent size. If you spot a parking to activate, stop and get it done...the next one won't be any better.

name: Riverton Wildlife Management Area
notes: Very well developed WMA, with several parking lots and large boat launch areas around the entire perimeter. most of the perimeter road is paved and parking lots are in good condition. Out-of-the-way, quiet park.

name: Toronto Springs State Conservation Area
notes: Two parking lots available, one off Hwy C (lower elevation) and the main one off Hwy A (higher elevation).

name: Rochester Falls State Conservation Area
notes: Only a river access, but nothing wrong with this park. Two parking lots...one is a circle parking with camping. Easy to find on the county hwy.

name: Hazel Hill Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Very nice lakeside conservation area with facilities, large boat launch and expansive parking area uphill from the dock. Easy to find

name: J.N. Turkey Kearn Memorial Wildlife Area
notes: This conservation area has four separate tracts. The main tract on the north side is the nicest. Several well-marked parking lots on the other tracts. Note this is in the Whiteman AFB flight path, so don't be surprised by jets overhead.

name: Ralph and Martha Perry Memorial State Wildlife Area
notes: Attractive area with prairies and lakes, parking lots, as well as a newly built DIY shooting range.

name: Connor O. Fewel State Conservation Area
notes: Two separate tracts of land with private land in between.

name: Flight Lake Conservation Reserve
notes: Basic conservation area with a few parking lots.

name: Huckleberry Ridge Conservation Reserve
notes: Generally featureless park...lots of roads, parking lots, etc.

name: Fort Crowder Conservation Reserve
notes: Generally featureless park...roads and parking lots on the entire perimeter. Easy to find.

name: Douglas Branch Conservation Reserve
notes: Don't blink or you'll miss it. Borders highway and is a smaller park with only one parking lot.

name: James R. Harter Conservation Reserve
notes: Basic no frills conservation area with one parking lot to activate. Easy to find off the highway.

name: Edward Anderson Conservation Reserve
notes: One of three Conservation Areas in a north-south line overlooking the river. Several parking lots and scenic pull-offs available...some inside the parks.

name: Dupont Reservation Conservation Reserve
notes: One of three Conservation Areas in a north-south line overlooking the river. Several parking lots and overlook pull-offs available...some inside the park.

name: Ted Shanks Conservation Reserve
notes: One of three Conservation Areas in a north-south line overlooking the river. Several parking lots and scenic overlooks available...some inside the park.

name: Davisdale Conservation Reserve
notes: Many perimeter parking lots and hiking trails. Larger park, but with a private tract in the middle...watch for signs...do not trespass.

name: Wellsville Lake Conservation Reserve
notes: Single access road and parking lot with boat launch. Fishing access and a DIY shooting range. Scenic small lake.

name: Little Lost Creek Conservation Reserve
notes: Bordered by two county roads on the west and east, several parking lots on either road. Some gravel roads and primitive camping in the park.

name: Flag Spring Conservation Reserve
notes: Only one main road with parking lots and a DIY shooting range. Also several trails with open areas.

name: Bittern Bottoms Conservation Reserve
notes: If you blink, you'll miss it. Small road-site parking lot and a hiking path into marshland rich in wildlife.

name: Dorsett Hill Prairie Conservation Reserve
notes: Easy to find the obvious parking lot and sign at county road intersection. Easy to activate from the parking lot. A pair of friendly local dogs like to hang out.

name: Sni-A Bar Conservation Reserve
notes: Don't blink or you'll miss it. No features, only a small MDC sign. Gate is in park so can be activated, but there is a clear hiking path into the park.

name: Liberty Bend Conservation Reserve
notes: The access parking lot is LaBenite Park. The conservation area is accessible by hiking path along the river for about 1/4 mile. LaBenite Park is NOT within the boundaries of the conservation reserve.

name: Maple Woods Natural Area
notes: This is an in-town park, residential area. In a bit of a "hollow". Popular spot for hiking/waling local population, so can be busy at peak times.

name: Foxglove Conservation Reserve
notes: Small park inside the bend in the road. One parking lot, easy to find, next to an open area...rural residential area. A few dogs may inspect you.

name: Pigeon Hill Conservation Reserve
notes: This is a primarily shooting range conservation area. Can be very busy at peak times. Suggest activating from the archery range parking lot which is separate from the rifle/piston range.

name: Lick Creek Conservation Reserve
notes: Quiet one-road, one parking lot park at lower elevation than surrounding region. Easy access to shore fishing before/after activating.

name: Moniteau Creek Conservation Reserve
notes: Very irregular shaped park. Research on Google Earth prior to activating to avoid private areas. Some parking lots.

name: Upper Mississippi Conservation Reserve
notes: There are several river access points, but check Google Earth to choose a spot ahead of activating.

name: William R Logan Conservation Reserve
notes: Three access roads and several parking lots. Also a DIY shooting range.

name: Ozark State Trail
notes: This park is under construction by at least three government agencies. The trail currently has over a dozen segments that will eventually be joined and continue into Arkansas. This trail goes through a number of other parks.

name: Taberville Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Textbook prairie land area. Nice parking lot, out in open prairie. Can activate from parking lot, or can be ideal for a hike in to some flat rock outcroppings in the middle of the park.

name: Elam Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Clean well-developed conservation area, with several parking lots and a DIY shooting range. Also boat ramp to the Grand River.

name: Adams Homestead State Nature Preserve
notes: No entrance fee required. Year-round. Between Oct. 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets and other water systems may be closed

name: Gallatin State Conservation Area
notes: Gives the impression of being a primarily shooting range conservation area...but clean and well-maintained DIY range for both shotgun and rifle/pistol. Two main parking lots. Easy to find.

name: Marais Temps Clair State Conservation Area
notes: Virtually 100% wetlands...pick your spot on Google Earth and pick your season so roads are acceptable.

name: Little Bean Marsh State Conservation Area
notes: Out-of-the-way park, easy to find. Large parking lot to activate from. Check first for seasonal flooding.

name: Paint Brush Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find on main hwy, but two other parking lots on the east and south borders.

name: Mine Creek Civil War Battlefield State Historic Site

name: Benedictine Bottoms State Wildlife Area

name: Pawnee Prairie State Natural Area
notes: Very open pure prairie park. The only parking lot is a few miles south of the small town and on the highest elevation spot for miles around.

name: Agency State Conservation Area
notes: Tiny, easy to miss, hard to find. Only one parking lot on a forested gravel road.

name: Arthur Dupree Memorial State Conservation Area

name: Aspinwall Bend State Conservation Area

name: Copan State Wildlife Area
