notes: The main entrance is on Charity Lake with parking area, open area and fishing access. The road that goes northwest of the lake stops at a higher elevation parking lot.

name: Corning State Conservation Area
notes: Suggest you research your route on Google Earth. Google Maps will get you lost on this one. Easiest to access from the nearby town of Corning.

name: Deroin Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Be advised that access is difficult due to construction. You may be able to get inside the boundary via some local roads. You may need an accurate map, SUV, and patience to get inside the boundary on this one. Or go by boat on the river.

name: Lower Hamburg Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Flood reconstruction continues, and only one open access road was found...it's the one that's on the state line into the northeast corner of the park and crosses over the levee. All other access roads are closed for construction or private property.

name: Rush Bottoms State Conservation Area
notes: Research your route on Google Earth for this one. Check website for flooding and other closures. Best access is the eastern river shore east of Rulo...underpass to the park levee to activate.

name: Star School Hill Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: This park has two tracts about two miles apart...each with a very small up-sloped parking lot. Not ideal activating except for a short time.

name: Wolf Creek Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find at the end of long gravel roads...but research your route on Google Earth for this one.

name: B.K. Leach Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: This is mostly a wetlands park...subject to seasonal flooding. Research or call ahead before a long drive.

name: Bee Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Don't blink or you'll miss it. Only one parking lot, not far off the main highway.

name: Bethel Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Relatively close to the highway, and a single parking lot on the southern border county road. Easy to find. Roads can be rough in the springtime.

name: Black Island State Conservation Area
notes: There are roads, but access to this area is not obvious. Plan you route on Google Earth before activating, and expect certain wetland features may change seasonally.

name: Bonanza State Conservation Area
notes: Park has two tracts, with the eastern tract being the most developed one. Surprisingly scenic in spite of the map. Several parking lots.

name: Bristow State Conservation Area
notes: One of the basic "square" prairie conservation areas...only one parking lot on the eat border. Easy to find.

name: Buffalo Wallow State Conservation Area
notes: This park has three discontinous tracts, but it can be tricky to find it. Not many signs. Need to research the park on Google Earth before you activate.

name: Bunch Hollow State Conservation Area
notes: Best to stay on the eastern roads/approaches. The west side can become impassable during wet seasons. Most of the parking lots and fishing spots are on the east side.

name: Caney State Conservation Area
notes: Larger hilly area with several roads and some parking lots, as well as hiking trails and camping. The east entrance is apparently not public, but there is a shooting range on the west entrance that is a good activating spot.

name: Clear Creek State Conservation Area
notes: This park is not well marked, irregularly shaped, so tricky to find it and it is surrounded by private lands. Research it on Google Earth!

name: Cuivre Island State Conservation Area
notes: Mainland tract is small with the only parking lot. The rest or the park consists of two forested islands.

name: Dorris Creek Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: One parking lot on the south western corner. Easy to find. Out of the way park. Open prairie.

name: Fourche Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Five separate tracts with no parking lots...be prepared for alternative activating techniques. Research your activating spot before you get there.

name: Girvin State Conservation Area
notes: The MDC asks that you stay off the access road when it is wet...which means seasonal access may be restricted...and only known when you get there. Plan activations during dry weather.

name: Honey Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Larger conservation area with equestrian themes and facilities. Large parking lots on higher elevations.

name: Ketcherside Mountain State Conservation Area
notes: This area has several separate tracts...some accessible on the Ozark Trail...some accessible by road. Very irregular outline bordered by private lands. Research carefully before activating.

name: Little Compton Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller park but very nice, clean and nice fishing lake with jetties. Two main parking lots on opposite shores.

name: Mincy State Conservation Area
notes: This is administratively ONE Conservation area that is split into two flanks. Lots of parking lots. Generally lower elevation and subject to flooding. Check before travel.

name: Mo-No-I Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find square conservation area. Road can be difficult in the spring. One parking lot on the southern border.

name: Monkey Mountain State Conservation Area
notes: Suggest activating of the parking lots on the north end of the park. Parking lots and roads on the south border are at lower elevations and in poor condition.

name: Osage Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find park, a few parking lots.

name: Pa Sole Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: A single parking lot area...open prairie. Easy to find. RF quiet spot.

name: Pelican Island State Conservation Area
notes: The very small boat launch and access area is the only accessible activation spot on the mainland. 95% of this park is island access by boat.

name: Ranacker State Conservation Area
notes: This is a lower elevation park. Several parking areas and access points. Features a DIY shooting range on the east access road.

name: Redwing Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: One parking lot on the southern border, but parking lot is tiny...first come, first served...

name: Riverbreaks State Conservation Area
notes: Several parking lots, open areas, primitive camping, and a large DIY shooting range.

name: Treaty Line State Conservation Area
notes: Large parking lot on the north-west corner...easy to find.

name: White Ranch State Conservation Area
notes: The lake parking lot at the center of the park is the best activating spot.

name: Worthwine Island State Conservation Area
notes: Two easy to find parking lots. Close to river so check website for flooding and other closures.

name: Yellow Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Only two parking lots off the west border gravel road. Can be dusty. Parking lots are tree-crowded.

name: Nishnabotna State Conservation Area
notes: The river levee is drive-on, so the levee is an ideal activation spot. Clear view to the horizon in all directions. Some primitive camping available.

name: Risch State Conservation Area
notes: Oddly shaped park, with the only parking lot at the southern tip of a long narrow section. Easy to miss. Google Maps will not take you there...research and plan on Google Earth!

name: Stoney Point Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Prairie park with a few parking lots. The northern border road parking lot is easiest to find.

name: Sky Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Small featureless prairie park with only one parking lot.

name: Bluff Springs State Conservation Area
notes: Only one parking lot off CR 724, with primitive camping. Basic forest/prairie park with no development.

name: Brush Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Basic square lot with one parking lot on the northwest corner.

name: Marion Bottoms State Conservation Area
notes: Check flood status before activating. Only two parking lots available...park may be inaccessible seasonally.

name: Three Creeks State Conservation Area
notes: A few roads with a few parking lots.

name: Buford Mountain State Conservation Area
notes: Primarily a hiking trail area with only one parking lot.

name: University Forest State Conservation Area
notes: This park is very irregular shaped and has separate tracts. Research carefully before activating.

name: Glenwood Archaeological State Historic Site
notes: Best activated from the parking lots. Open areas may be sensitive to archeology finds. If you intend to hike in, best to ask at the ranger station.

name: Birdsong State Conservation Area
notes: Two tracts of land. Northwestern tract has three parking lots and primitive camping sites.

name: Little River State Conservation Area
notes: This is primarily a waterfowl development area and wetlands. See website for possible flooding closures and restrictions to certain pools.

name: Hornersville State Conservation Area
notes: Check website for various closures for wildlife management reasons.

name: Ripgut Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: The only parking lot and best access is on the southern boundary. Google Maps won't take you there...chart your route on Google Earth.

name: Old Town Access State Conservation Area
notes: Even though this is "only" a river access, it has as much land and good parking lots as many other Conservation Areas. Check before activating for flooding/access.

name: McGee Family State Conservation Area
notes: Modest Conservation Area, with a few parking lots to activate. Small ponds sprinkled around the park.

name: Pilot Knob State Conservation Area
notes: This State Conservation Area also has a SOTA summit WØM/ES-003, that can be activated by hiking up the hill. Access hiking trail from the north and west borders. Parking lot on the west border.

name: Dr Harry and Lina Berrier Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: Newly-created...small parking lot with a sign adjacent to a private drive. Hiking path to prairie heading east from the parking lot.

name: Urich State Conservation Area
notes: Basic conservation area. Two main access areas and parking lots. Small parking lot on west side. Larger, nicer parking lot on the east side. Easy to find not far off the highway.

name: Pacific Palisades State Conservation Area
notes: Two access roads and two parking lots. Primarily a bird hunting area.

name: Rockwoods State Conservation Area
notes: Several access roads and parking lots, some trails and a pavillion.

name: Mussel Fork State Conservation Area
notes: Large Conservation Area, next to Hwy 36. Parking lot about 100 yds from Hwy 36 on Noble Drive. Not scenic, but it works. Deeper in the park, there are small fishing ponds and other recreational facilities.

name: Union Ridge State Conservation Area
notes: Larger Conservation Area with multiple access points and parking lots. If you don't like one, just drive another mile to the next one. Some parking lots at higher elevations, some in valleys.

name: Sugar Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Typical conservation area with forests and prairie, several parking lots and a DIY shooting range.

name: Indian Hills State Conservation Area
notes: Several parking lots and some primitive camping areas.

name: Hidden Hollow State Conservation Area
notes: Wooded park with three parking lots, and a few roads.

name: LaBarque Creek State Conservation Area
notes: One parking lot and some hiking trails.

name: Big Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Some perimeter parking lots, hiking trails.

name: Shoemaker State Conservation Area
notes: Small generic Conservation Area...two small parking lots. Easy to miss.

name: Ruth and Paul Henning Conservation Area State Conservation Area
notes: This Conservation Area surrounds (but, oddly, does not include) the White River Balds Natural Area. Several good parking lots and access points. Easy to find.

name: White River Balds Natural Area State Conservation Area
notes: This Natural Area is included but not part of K-8510. It is managed by K-8510. Generally higher elevation. Proximity to tourist areas, so can be busy.

name: Springfield Conservation Nature Center State Conservation Area
notes: In-town park with large parking lot and several manicured walking trails...some open area. Can be very busy during peak times.

name: Wood River West Wildlife Management Area
Constitution Hall State Historic Site
notes: This is a small in-town park. There is an accessible parking lot in the back yard from the laneway that has been used for activating on Mondays and Tuesdays and hours when the museum is closed. Otherwise ask for permission to set up.

name: Fort Hays State Historic Site
notes: Open 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Wednesday - Saturday. See website for further information.

name: Grinter Place State Historic Site
notes: Very large parking lot up high and in the clear. Easy to find next to the main road and not far from HWY 435.

name: Hollenberg Pony Express Station State Historic Site
notes: Nice park out in middle of prairie expanse. Very nice open area and elevated (as far as can be in KS) parking lot to activate from.

name: Kaw Mission State Historic Site
notes: Building is temporarily closed. Parking is available in front of the Mission.

name: Pawnee Indian Museum State Historic Site
notes: Grounds are open even though the museum building may not be. Extensive walking paths and manicured grounds...large paved parking lot.

name: Red Rocks State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park...very tiny garage entrance parking for one vehicle. However, the road in front of the building has a sign that restricts parking to Historic Site visitors only, and the historical marker is on the curb.

name: Cottonwood Ranch State Historic Site
notes: The exterior of the property is open dawn until dusk, daily. The ranch house itself is available for guided tours only.

name: First Territorial Capitol State Historic Site
notes: This park in on a military station. Access is restricted/controlled, but possible as long as the published procedure is followed. Military ID preferred, but civilians with specified documents can access. Read information carefully before attempting.

name: Goodnow House State Historic Site
notes: Open daily 9:00 - 5:00 Tuesday through Friday. Open 2:00 - 5:00 Saturday & Sunday. Closed holidays.

name: John Brown Museum State Historic Site
notes: This park is in town, but the grounds are large and the various parking lots are good size. The west side closest to the museum is higher elevation. Noise levels not too bad for in-town.

name: Shawnee Indian Mission State Historic Site
notes: Small limited parking lot in a residential area. Mobile activation favored. Very limited open space around the yard for other options.

name: Iowa and Sac & Fox Mission State Historic Site
notes: Small property at the end of a laneway. Parking lot and one picnic table. Can be semi-abandoned certain times of the year, but otherwise easy to find and access.

name: Marais des Cygnes Massacre State Historic Site
notes: Out-of-the-way park on gravel roads, but the park area itself is on an elevated bluff, obvious sign, with picnic tables and open areas to activate. Some park roadways may be washed out by rain, so be cautious.

name: Pawnee Rock State Historic Site
notes: Parking available.

name: Hendrickson Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Wildlife management area surrounding Hendrickson Marsh Lake. Several gravel parking areas and a boat launch.

name: Colfax Wildlife Management Area
notes: The park is best found on maps...the DNR website is not very detailed on this one. A variety of hunting websites show it well. It is very poorly identified, so be sure where you are.

name: Redbird Farms Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA is on both sides of the road and each side has parking for activations.

name: Hawkeye Wildlife Management Area
notes: NOTE: Most of the land here is US Army Corps of Engineers which is OUTSIDE of the POTA entity. A small section is state owned and valid for POTA. See the map to the assessor's page. Do not operate on USACE land. The pin on the POTA map is accurate.

name: Hanging Rock Ridge Wildlife Management Area
notes: Relatively small WMA with a single parking lot.

name: Salt Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small, wooded WMA hunting area with a single parking entrance on the south side.

name: Hawthorne Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small WMA lake with several parking areas for activations.

name: Fox River Wildlife Management Area
notes: As with all Refuges, no impact setup and small footprints are best. Reasonably well identified and good parking lots.

name: Lake Sugema Wildlife Management Area
notes: K-4573 intersects some areas of this WMA for a possible 2-fer. Check the K-4573 map for details.

name: Sand Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Easy to miss. Roads can be rough by season.

name: Fogle Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Rural WMA with a parking area for activation. Note that the WMA is adjacent to a county park with the Fogle Lake name. Check the DNR map for the location of the WMA.

name: Kellerton Bird Wildlife Management Area
notes: Bird conservation area near Kellerton. Private property around, so please research before activating.

name: Lake Shawtee Wildlife Management Area
notes: Wildlife area - public hunting grounds. Relatively elevated parking areas from surrounding terrain are great for activations.

name: Cooper Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Easy to find with Google Maps/GPS, but very little signage. One parking area on the east border with DNR signs. Easy to activate, out of the way, quiet.

name: Forney's Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Large WMA, but no visible lake other than an expansive marsh. Some parking lots on the south and east borders, but the main circle parking is on the south border.

name: Green Hollow Wildlife Management Area
notes: Although the map does not show it, there is a parking lot about half-way up the east border road. This parking lot has the WMA sign and is at a high elevation spot for the area/park. Ideal activation spot.

name: St Mary's Island Wildlife Management Area
notes: Research/plan carefully on Google Earth and DNR maps before activating...some accesses are better than others.

name: Nobles Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small parking lot next to an oxbow lake. Simple small park...no frills, but peaceful and easy to find.

name: Keg Creek lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Nice, straightforward, smaller park in view of the highway. Small parking lot overlooking a small pond. Easy to find.

name: Rosenow Timber Wildlife Management Area
notes: Forest WMA with limited parking spots.

name: Round Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: A small parking lot off the rural road...well-marked, but easy to miss if you are not looking for it.

name: Beaver Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Typical WMA with nice lake and parking lots. The DNR site mentions picnic areas but there are no picnic tables. There is a campground adjacent to but not within the park.

name: Three Mile Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Parking for the WMA on the West and South sides of the lake. The County Parks on the North and East sides of the lake are not within the WMA. A 2-fer is possible with K-4573 only at the area east of the intersection of 12 Mile Lake Ave and 148th St.

name: Elk Grove Wildlife Management Area
notes: Forested WMA - hunting area with several gravel parking area for activations.

name: Harrier Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Not hard to find. As this is part of the US FWS system, it also counts for US-0270. Check the maps for both.

name: Finn Pond Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small WMA parking lot next to highway.

name: Goose Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small lake surrounded by wildlife management area. Parking areas and boat launches available for activations.

name: Tomahawk Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Several small parking lots, easy to miss. Google may take you to a parking lot that is actually private property. Be sure to activate from the public hunting lot.

name: Big Sioux River Wildlife Management Area
notes: This WMA has a chain of 4 units along the Big Sioux River. Typical WMA parking is available for activations.

name: Morse Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small lake with access road along east side of lake. Parking / boat launch on south side works for POTA.

name: Lower Morse Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Typical Iowa DNR wildlife management area. Note that the parking lot is marked on the map for this location. As this is part of the US FWS Iowa Wetland Management District, it also counts for US-0270.

name: Elm Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: There are two public access boat launch areas for this lake. The launch at the north end isolated... a good spot for POTA. The launch on the east side of the lake is surrounded by houses. DNR officer also recommended the north spot was best for POTA.

name: Buffalo Basins Wildlife Management Area
notes: DNR wildlife area. Grass parking entrance is on highway (Balsam Ave) along the west edge of the WMA.

name: Waterman Prarie Complex Wildlife Management Area
notes: Well-marked parking lot on the road to Peterson, but not obvious to find. It is in a valley.

name: Wittrock Indian Village State Preserve
notes: Not well-marked archeology site. Must hike (~.5 mi) to reach the State Preserve from the East. There is a small indent off the road at the bottom of the hill. Suggest parking on the road and hiking in to be in boundary. Private land East and North.

name: Little Storm Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: The parking lot and sign are on the inside of a busy local street, across from the beach park. Suggest turning into the beach park and then crossing to the WMA parking when traffic allows. Otherwise, small dirt parking lot, no frills.

name: Rush Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Well-marked on roadside, but only a rough parking lot at the end of a two-rut dirt road...lots of wildlife. This site is in Osceola county near Ocheyedan. Another area named Rush Lake is in Palo Alto county.

name: Deweys Pasture Wildlife Management Area
notes: Need to research the boundaries carefully, but Dewey and Barringers are across the road from each other.

name: Eagle Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Fishing area in Hancock county. At least two parking areas for activations. As this is part of the US FWS Iowa Wetland Management District, it also counts for K-0270.

name: Blue Wing Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with private property nearby. Please research before activating. There are more than two locations in Iowa called "Blue Wing Marsh", but only this one is managed by Iowa DNR.

name: Barringers Slough Wildlife Management Area
notes: Need to research maps carefully, but Dewey and Barringers are across the road from each other at one spot.

name: Teal Basins State Waterfowl Management Area
notes: Pheasant hunting grounds with a single gravel parking area on the South side of the Waterfowl Production Area. As this is part of the US FWS Iowa Wetland Management District, it also counts for K-0270.

name: Wapsi Flats Wildlife Management Area
notes: Rural WMA hunting grounds with 2 sections. Small gravel parking lots.

name: Sweet Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with several parking locations for activations including a boat ramp on the south end.

name: Turkey River Wildlife Management Area
notes: Southern parking area on King's Road in the middle of this WMA is easily accessed. If not available, there are two additional parking areas at the north end of the WMA.

name: Cardinal Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA along the Turkey River with several parking areas.

name: Bluffton Fir Stand State Preserve
notes: Public hunting grounds surrounding the town of Bluffton. Several parking lots / boat launches are within the preserve.

name: Pine Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Parking lot down in the valley on the east end of the WMA or off the road that borders the south

name: Coon Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: 3 parking areas for this WMA. The lot on the SouthWest side of the WMA is not near the creek itself but is substantially more elevated than the other 2.

name: South Pine Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Gravel parking lot access to WMA.

name: Canoe Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Parking at the confluence of Canoe Creek and Upper Iowa River. Busy area during fishing season.

name: North Bear Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: 5 parking lots along the creek for this WMA. This entity is adjacent to South Bear Creek WMA. They do not overlap.

name: South Bear Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: 7 parking lots along the South Bear Creek WMA.

name: Big Mill Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Trout stream WMA. Parking areas for activation at both the north and south end of the WMA.

name: Barber Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Public hunting area north of the Wapsipinicon River. A few parking areas along a gravel road.

name: Lost Grove Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: DNR lake with surrounding WMA (restored prairie). Several boat launches and parking areas available.

name: Wiese Slough Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA along Cedar River with 4 parking areas and two boat ramps that may provide activation areas.

name: Red Cedar Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA along Cedar River near Cedar Bottoms WMA (K-9352). At least 2 parking areas on north side may be locations for activations.

name: Cedar Bottoms Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA is divided into 2 sections (on either side of Cedar River). Parking areas available on both may provide activation areas.

name: Cone Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with small parking lots and 2 boat ramps for activation areas.

name: Fox Hills Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with 2 sections along the river. At least 3 parking areas listed for potential activation spots. Forested, with private land nearby. Some parking areas are very small. Check the DNR maps not just Google maps for this one.

name: Danish Alps State Recreation Area
notes: Very nice lakeshore rec area...several potential activating spots. A park entry permit is required, so combining activating other nearby parks like Ponca SP is suggested.

name: Lewis and Clark Lake State Recreation Area
Riverview State Recreation Area
notes: Do not follow Google Maps/GPS that follows a private industrial road along the river...instead start from downtown Neb City and go east from there through residential areas. Park permit is required and must be purchased off-site ahead of arrival.

name: Rock Creek Station State Recreation Area
notes: Park does NOT share land with K-2623. K-4578 does not go through this entity. No dual/triple activation possible. Vehicle entry fee required.

name: Rockford Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Park access fee required for this park. Purchase on-line or locally ahead of time.

name: Lehigh Portland State Park
notes: Very new park in Kansas. Used to be a local trails park by the same name. Website and maps show it officially, but likely more well-defined maps to become available soon.

name: Katy Trail Rock Island Spur State Park
notes: Very new State Park. Used to be the Rock Island Spur of the Katy Trail State Park. This is a new, separate trail park, so not a 2-fer with Katy Trail...and the pin is placed at trail head in Windsor.

name: Butterfield Overland National Historic Trail
notes: This is a very new NHT created in 2023. Please be aware that it will be some time before official trail markers appear, and as with all NHTs, activation must be on public property, even though much of the trail is on private lands. Research carefully!

name: Boone Forks Wildlife Management Area
notes: Wildlife management area along the river in several sections with multiple parking & activation spots. 4666 acres. Private property in the area so research first.

name: Colo Bogs Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with several parking areas for activation.

name: Iowa River Corridor Wildlife Area
notes: Large (10000 acre) WMA along the Iowa River with many parking lots - activation points available between Tama and Marengo. Meskwaki Nation is West of Tama, so you might consider activating to the South East of Tama to ensure you're on USFWS land.

name: Wapello Bottoms Wildlife Area
notes: WMA along Mississippi

name: Bob Pyle Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small WMA with a single parking area for activations at the north end.

name: Wire Road State Conservation Area
notes: Possible that Trail of Tears and Butterfield Trails go through this property. Research carefully.

name: Kings Prairie Access State Conservation Area
Blue Spring Branch State Conservation Area
Lake City Range State Recreation Site
notes: Note that this is a staffed shooting range, unlike the numerous DIY ranges in the Conservation Areas. Suggest activating from parking lot farthest from building or ranges. There WILL be shooting noise. Pay attention to hours of operation.

name: Tower Rock State Natural Area
notes: Comply with MDC access instructions and warnings and access dates.

name: Perry Tower Site State Conservation Area
Marble Beach State Recreation Area
notes: State recreation area beach along the west shore of Spirit Lake. Campground.

name: Smoky Waters State Conservation Area
notes: Note that this area has two separate tracts with private land between them. Observe all access instructions and respect private/posted lands.

name: Hart Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Note that the Katy Trail forms the west boundary to this park, adjacent to this park, but is not a 2-fer with this park.

name: Gist Ranch State Conservation Area
notes: Larger SCA, includes a shooting range.

name: Sunklands State Conservation Area
notes: This is a huge conservation area...may be several access areas. Research carefully.

name: Mon-Shon State Conservation Area
notes: Lots of farming industry across the road, so the park can be RF-noisy.

name: Capps Creek State Conservation Area
notes: This park has some small private tracts and cemeteries...please be respectful

name: Niangua State Conservation Area
notes: This park has three small separate tracts...research carefully and know where you are.

name: Robert E. Talbot State Conservation Area
notes: This is a large park with separate tracts with private lands in between. Research carefully and know where you are.

name: The Lewis Family, Dean, Anna Mae and David D. Lewis State Conservation Area
Delaware Town Access State Conservation Area
Lower Flat Creek Access State Conservation Area
notes: This park is tiny, so pay attention to adjacent posted or private land.

name: Shelvin Rock Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small access area with limited parking. Be mindful that boat access is the primary use of this site, and that activation can possibly be difficult at peak seasons/times.

name: Saline Valley State Conservation Area
notes: Large irregular-shaped park...research carefully and know where you are.

name: Victoria Glades State Conservation Area
notes: This is a park with a small parking lot ACROSS from the park/trailhead. The parking lot may be owned by the park if there is a sign. If the sign is on the west side of the road, then likely the parking lot is not in the park.

name: Valley View Glades State Conservation Area
notes: Only one parking lot (trail head) and long trails.

name: Mammoth Access State Conservation Area
notes: Small river access. Please be mindful of primary users during busy times.

name: Myron and Sonya Glassberg Family State Conservation Area
Plowboy Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Pay attention to the private parcel of land at the middle of the park.

name: Roger V. and Viola Wachal Smith State Conservation Area
Chichaqua Wildlife Area
notes: Wildlife area. Note that there is also county conservation grounds in the area which is not within the boundary of the POTA entity. Check the map and be sure you are within the boundary of the Iowa DNR owned and managed site.

name: South Scalp Creek State Recreation Area
Joe Day Bay State Recreation Area
Tabor State Recreation Area
notes: On a minimum maintenance road requiring high clearance vehicle when road is wet or muddy.

name: Dodge Draw State Vehicle Recreational Area
Joe Crighton Beach Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park along the beach. Please be respectful of adjacent residences and other patrons when activating!

name: Rocky Mount Tower Site State Conservation Area
notes: Not much parking outside the gate, but plenty of setup room around the tower site. Tower has been removed but the four leg bases are still there.

name: Scrivner Road State Conservation Area
notes: Includes a very large and busy DIY shooting range. Best activating locations on the hill, northwest of the range, around the maintenance barn.

name: Little Sac Woods State Conservation Area
Coldwater State Conservation Area
notes: This park has multiple tracts separated by private lands. Please research the website maps and be certain of your location before activating.

name: Lipton State Conservation Area
notes: This area's trailhead is on city Santa Fe Park property, north of the road. The State Conservation area is south of the trailhead/road ONLY (past the MDC sign) The park can NOT be activated from the city park's parking lot! This is a hike-in only park.

name: Walnut Woods State Conservation Area
notes: This park is ONLY accessible by hiking through Ruth Stockdale Park (which is a city park). This park can NOT be activated from the city park's parking lot! This is a hike-in ONLY park.

name: Rush Creek State Conservation Area
notes: This park is ONLY accessible by hiking THROUGH the non-POTA Martha Lafite Thompson Nature Sanctuary. This park CANNOT be activated from the city-owned Nature Sanctuary's parking lot! The scenic overlook is at the end of a 1/4 mile paved trail.

name: Pigg's Landing Access State Conservation Area
notes: Not a very large park...please be respectful of primary users during peak/busy times.

name: Schimmel City Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park. Please be respectful of primary users during peak/busy times.

name: Dr. Frederick Marshall State Conservation Area
La Due Bottoms State Conservation Area
notes: This park has three separate tracts. The western tracts, closest to La Due are dry land, good signage and a parking lot. The east tract is waterfowl marsh and access may be seasonal.

name: Kearn Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: There are several parks in this area with the name "Kearn" in them. These are not duplicates, nor are they 2-fers. Research carefully before activating.

name: Bryson's Hope State Conservation Area
notes: This park is adjacent to Kearn Memorial, but is NOT a 2-fer with it.

name: Gama Grass Prairie State Conservation Area
Youngdahl Urban State Conservation Area
notes: This is a in-city park. Please use small station footprints.

name: Blue Lick State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find, good parking lot to activate from.

name: Spring Creek Gap State Conservation Area
Roselle Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park. Please be respectful of the primary users during peak/busy times.

name: Marquand Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park. Please be respectful of the primary users during peak/busy times.

name: Thompson Ford Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park. Please be respectful of the primary users during peak/busy times.

name: Tolona Access State Conservation Area
notes: Small park. Be mindful and courteous of/to primary users during busy or peak times.

name: Sunnyside School Access State Conservation Area
notes: Small Park. Be respectful of primary users during busy or peak times.

name: White Oak Bend Access State Conservation Area
notes: Small park. Be respectful of primary users during busy or peak times.

name: Ella Ewing Lake State Conservation Area
Clark State Conservation Area
notes: This park has several separate tracts. Research carefully before activation so you KNOW where you are.

name: Charlie Heath Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: Larger park that is spread along the rivers. Research carefully so you KNOW where you are. The river flows across private land at one point.

name: Forest 44 State Conservation Area
notes: This park is extensively a hiking trail park with a parking lot and a DIY shooting range in a restricted use area. Research carefully.

name: Wayne Helton Memorial State Conservation Area
Ten Mile Pond State Conservation Area
notes: This park has extensive and complex shooting and hunting zones according to dates and seasons. Research carefully before activating! The only non-shooting/hunting zone is the ranger station...probably the best activating location.

name: Little Indian Creek State Conservation Area
Pea Ridge State Conservation Area
notes: This park has five(5) separate tracts...please research carefully before activating to KNOW where you are.

name: Woodson K Woods Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: This park borders Meramec Springs Park to NW and SE...which is NOT a POTA park. Research carefully before activating.

name: White River Trace State Conservation Area
Gerhild and Graham Brown State Conservation Area
Robert H. Thompson State Conservation Area
notes: This park is a hike-in ONLY park. The available ACOE boat ramp and parking lot that is north of the park is NOT part of the park. Foot traffic is welcome along shoreline, but check local river levels, as this park is prone to flooding.

name: Cephas Ford Access State Conservation Area
notes: Across the highway from Douglas SCA

name: McCoy Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with 2 parking areas. Check maps as there is private and ACOE land nearby.

name: Old Plantation Access State Conservation Area
notes: This park has limited parking. Please be considerate of primary users during peak or busy seasons and times.

name: Maintz Wildlife Reserve
notes: This park has carved out private tracts. Please research carefully to know where you are when activating.

name: Block Hole Access State Conservation Area
notes: Very limited parking space, especially at peak seasons and times. Please be respectful of primary users when activating.

name: Tywappity Community Lake State Conservation Area
notes: This land was acquired by the Missouri Dept of Conservation in 1957, so ALL MDC rules and regulations apply.

name: Harry S Truman Home National Historical Site
notes: Urban site- no street parking. Most of the sub-sites are secured 24/7. Activating is possible ONLY from the Noland Home site, on the west side of Delaware St. Please be mindful of and comply with ranger/website instructions! High RF noise area.

name: Diamond Grove Prairie State Conservation Area
Marguerite Bray State Conservation Area
notes: This is a smaller park with limited space to park. Please be mindful of other patrons during busy or peak times.

name: Beaver Creek State Conservation Area
notes: This site requires some special permits to access under certain conditions. Please research the site carefully before activating.

name: Blue Jay Trail Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park with limited parking. Please be respectful to primary users during busy or peak times.

name: Miami Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a small park, so be respectful to primary users at busy or peak times. Nice close-up scenic view of the Missouri River.

name: McKinny State Conservation Area
notes: The parking lot appears to be on the lee side of any cell service towers, so no cell service.

name: Grandfather Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find...parking lot next to road. S7-S8 RF noise, unfortunately...sounds like cattle fence or leaky insulator.

name: Caroline Sheridan Logan Memorial Wildlife Area
notes: Not a 2-fer with K-11039! ONLY accessible on FOOT through forest and over a bluff. NO TRAILS. From the Sunbridge CA trail north turn, head thru forest approx 1200 ft on heading of 040 degrees. Preset GPS and research carefully to avoid private lands!
